A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give a unified framework that can achieve the best of the two worlds --- the approximation guarantee for the non-sparse case and the accuracy guarantee for the sparse case.

we show the following: (i) for arbitrary queries, the best known upper bound for the mean squared error is ~O(n2), and this bound is tight up to logarithmic factor; (ii) for counting queries, the best upper bound is ~O(√(n)), and this bound is also tight up to logarithms; and (iii) for sparse linear queries, the best approximation guarantee is polylogarithmic, and this bound is optimal up to logarithmic terms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry of differential privacy is rich and interesting and has connections with other areas of mathematics, such as discrepancy theory, linear regression, and the geometry of convex hulls.

for a wide class of queries, the mean squared error for differentially private mechanisms is closely related to the hereditary lower bound for the discrepancy of the corresponding set of linear queries.
the Gaussian mechanism is not just a simple tool, but a versatile and powerful technique for differentially private analysis.
